question: Who among the following novelists wrote ‘Midnight’s Children’?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Salman Rushdie**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Salman Rushdie is an Indian-born British-American novelist renowned for his distinctive blend of magic realism and historical fiction.
 
• His literary themes frequently explore the interplay, disruptions, and migrations between Eastern and Western civilizations, with a particular focus on the Indian subcontinent.
 
• Rushdie's second novel, "Midnight's Children" (1981), achieved widespread acclaim and secured the prestigious Booker Prize in 1981.
 
• It was twice recognized as "the best novel of all winners" on the 25th and 40th anniversaries of the prize, underscoring its enduring significance in the literary landscape. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Shashi Tharoor

 
 
• He is a Member of Parliament, Lok Sabha from Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala.
 
• He is former under Secretary-General of the United Nations for Communications and Public Information.
 
• Famous books:
 
 

 
• Bookless in Baghdad
 
• India from Midnight to Millennium
 
• Inglorious Empire
 
• The Paradoxical Prime Minister
 
• Why I Am a Hindu
 
• Nehru: The Invention of India

 
• **VS Naipaul**

 
 
• VS Naipaul won the Nobel Prize for Literature in 2001 for having a united perceptive narrative and incorruptible scrutiny in works that compel us to see the presence of suppressed histories.
 
 
 
• **Vikram Seth**
 
 
• Vikram Seth is a poet and novelist from India. 
 
• He has won numerous honours, including the Crossword Book Award, WH Smith Literary Award, Pravasi Bharatiya Samman, Sahitya Academy Award, and Padma Shri.
 
• Seth's poetry collections include works such as Mappings and Beastly Tales.
 
• After the release of A Suitable Boy, Seth gained widespread attention.
 
• In 2020, a BBC television drama miniseries based on it was produced.
